fixes.old: The il/elle form has no ending at all: the stem simply stands alone (il vend, il attend, il repond).
fixes.new: The il/elle form has no ending at all: the stem simply stands alone (il vend, il attend, il répond).
fixes.why: Missing acute accent on répond in the note.

fixes.old: The v surfaces in the plural; decrire and s'inscrire follow.
fixes.new: The v surfaces in the plural; décrire and s'inscrire follow.
fixes.why: Missing acute accent on décrire in the note.

fixes.old: Plural stem lis-, so nous lisons has one s sound, not a z.
fixes.new: Plural stem lis-, and a single s between two vowels is voiced: nous lisons sounds like li-zon.
fixes.why: Pronunciation stated backwards - nous lisons is [lizɔ̃], the s IS a z sound.

fixes.old: Direct consequence of the 1905 law separating Church and State.
fixes.new: The rule dates from the Revolution (1792), which secularised civil status; the 1905 law later separated Church and State.
fixes.why: Compulsory civil marriage predates 1905 - it comes from the 1791-92 secularisation of état civil.

fixes.old: the high-speed train (train à grande vitesse). Ex. : On met deux heures en TGV entre Paris et Marseille.
fixes.new: the high-speed train (train à grande vitesse). Ex. : On met trois heures en TGV entre Paris et Marseille.
fixes.why: Paris-Marseille by TGV takes about three hours, not two (two hours is Paris-Lyon).

fixes.old: The free-response half is now entirely built around your own project, so preparation you do in advance is worth 35% of the exam.
fixes.new: Two of the three free-response tasks are built around your own project, so preparation you do in advance is worth 35% of the exam.
fixes.why: The Argumentative Essay (15%) is not project-based, so the free-response half is not 'entirely' project-built.

fixes.old: 1) Politeness (je voudrais, pourriez-vous); 2) a hypothetical result after a si + imperfect clause; 3) unvérified or reported information in journalism (le nombre de victimes serait de dix); 4) wishes and suggestions (on pourrait, il faudrait).
fixes.new: 1) Politeness (je voudrais, pourriez-vous); 2) a hypothetical result after a si + imperfect clause; 3) unverified or reported information in journalism (le nombre de victimes serait de dix); 4) wishes and suggestions (on pourrait, il faudrait).
fixes.why: English word 'unverified' carries a stray French accent.

fixes.old: Feminine as a single work; masculine when it means the complete body of work: le grand œuvre.
fixes.new: Feminine in normal use, including l'œuvre de Camus for a whole body of work; masculine only in fixed expressions such as le grand œuvre, le gros œuvre and l'œuvre gravé de Rembrandt.
fixes.why: Note contradicts the card's own answer: 'an artist's whole output' is normally feminine (l'œuvre de Hugo); the masculine is restricted to fixed art/building phrases.
